steps.title: Open the terminal
steps.say: Press **Ctrl+`** (the key just above Tab, on the left). A panel slides up at the bottom: that's the **terminal**. Click somewhere in the editor first, so it hears your keys.

steps.title: Commands
steps.say: In the terminal you type a **command** and press **Enter**. The computer does it and tells you the result. Here are five to try. (They're the same files you see in the Explorer. The terminal is just another way to work with them.)

board.code:
pwd
ls
ls my-team
cat my-team/about.txt
mkdir practice

marks.label: show the words in a file

steps.title: Where am I?
steps.say: Click in the terminal, type `pwd` and press **Enter**. It prints the **path** of the folder you're in. That's your project folder.

steps.title: What's here?
steps.say: Type `ls` and press **Enter**. It **l**i**s**ts the files and folders here. They match the Explorer.

steps.title: Look inside a folder
steps.say: Type `ls my-team` and press **Enter**. You'll see what's inside the folder you made. (If it says no such file, make my-team with the **Make a folder and a file** guide.)

waitFor.hint: type ls my-team and press Enter.

steps.title: Read a file
steps.say: Type `cat my-team/about.txt` and press **Enter**. It shows the words in your file. The path tells it which file.

waitFor.hint: type cat my-team/about.txt and press Enter.

steps.title: Make a folder
steps.say: Type `mkdir practice` and press **Enter**. Then watch the Explorer on the left: a new folder appears by itself.

waitFor.hint: type mkdir practice and press Enter.

steps.title: Tidy up
steps.say: Let's remove it again. Type `rmdir practice` and press **Enter**. It disappears from the Explorer.

waitFor.hint: type rmdir practice and press Enter.

steps.title: Two handy tricks
steps.say: Press the **up arrow** in the terminal to bring back your last command, so you don't have to retype it. And press **Tab** while typing a name to let the terminal finish it for you.
